accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the accused blamed the intended target (PW-14, the shop owner and employer of the deceased) for interfering in his marital affairs and threatened to kill him; the deceased was an employee and an unintended victim
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.307, s.427 each read with s.34; Explosive Substances Act 1908 s.3 read with s.34 IPC
evidence_type: Approver (accomplice) testimony; eyewitness and injured-witness depositions; medical evidence; forensic (FSL) evidence; extrajudicial confession evidence via a witness; recovery/investigation evidence (purchase of gelatin sticks, detonators and tape recorder)
confession: Alleged extrajudicial confession by A-1 and A-2 to PW-3 (a relative) that they planted the bomb; the trial court relied on it as independent corroboration. Approver A-3's testimony was also relied on.
aggravating_circumstances: Use of an explosive device in a shop; death of an innocent employee; injuries to two other employees
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC: life rigorous imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine; s.307 r/w s.34: five years RI and Rs.1,000 fine; s.427 r/w s.34: one year RI; Explosive Substances Act s.3 r/w s.34: ten years RI and Rs.2,000 fine
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentences upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; attempt to murder under s.307 r/w s.34 IPC; mischief under s.427 r/w s.34 IPC; Explosive Substances Act s.3 r/w s.34 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that two accused, acting with a third person who later became an accomplice prosecution witness, planned to kill the owner of a hair salon whom they blamed for interfering in one accused's marital troubles. One accused had threatened to kill the owner within a week, and the other joined in that threat. The third person allegedly left a cardboard box containing a tape recorder loaded with explosive at the salon, saying he would return for it. Shortly afterwards, an employee switched on the device, which exploded with a loud sound, damaging the premises. The employee died from his injuries, and two other employees were injured. The prosecution relied on the accomplice's account; the testimony of a relative who said he saw the accused collect the box, pay for it and later hear them admit planting a bomb; the statements of the injured; and a doctor who described the injuries as caused by the blast. Forensic analysis of recovered debris and clothing reportedly detected nitroglycerine, nitrocellulose and ammonium nitrate. Investigators also found that gelatin sticks and detonators had been bought and that a tape recorder had been purchased from a shop.
physical_harm: Death of one employee (the deceased, Shankar); injuries to two other employees (PW-1 and PW-7) from the blast
financial_property_loss: Damage to the shop and several articles; value not stated
premeditation_planning: Yes. The court found the bomb was deliberately planted to kill the owner, with a co-accused deputed to carry the box to the shop and leave it there on a pretext.
motive: Domestic/marital grievance: A-1 blamed the shop owner (PW-14) for interfering in his marital affairs and threatened to kill him; A-2 joined the threat. Accepted by the courts as established.
key_evidence_accepted: Approver PW-2's testimony, corroborated by PW-3's deposition (box handover and confession), PW-1, PW-4, PW-7, PW-8, PW-9, PW-10, PW-11, PW-21 (FSL report of explosive residues) and PW-27 (medical evidence of blast injuries)
witness_credibility: The High Court found PW-3 credible with no reason to implicate the accused falsely; the trial court found the approver's version corroborated and the cross-examination did not discredit the medical and forensic witnesses. The Supreme Court accepted these concurrent findings.
post_offence_conduct: Per the trial court, the accused told witnesses after leaving the box that they had kept a bomb to kill their enemy and threatened them not to disclose it
custody_duration: About 12 years in custody as of 13 March 2012 (per the State's communication noted by the Court)
trial_duration: offence: 2 April 1996; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 16.03.2004; Supreme Court: 8 January 2013
legal_representation: Appellant: Tanuj Bagga Sharma (Amicus Curiae). State: Gurudatta Ankolekar, Azeem A. Kalebudde, V.N. Raghupathy and Sanjay R. Hedge for the respondent.
investigation_status: FIR lodged by PW-1; investigation by CCB police; chargesheet filed; committal after pardon to an accomplice; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted on all counts and sentenced. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
defence_argument: The approver's evidence was uncorroborated in material particulars, so the appellant should be acquitted.
legal_principle_applied: Under s.133 Evidence Act a conviction is not illegal merely on uncorroborated accomplice testimony, but the rule of practice (treated as a rule of law) requires corroboration in material particulars by untainted, credible evidence before convicting on an approver's evidence. Concurrent findings of fact on evidence not perverse, so no interference.
